props.title: Build Your Own
props.sub: From a first strategy to an AI agent

props.title: Your bot is the six boxes, in code
props.caption: Same six boxes as part one — now each becomes a small, testable function.

props.title: Get clean price data — for free
lines: # Indian stocks use the .NS suffix on NSE

side.title: The rules of data
points: Garbage in, garbage out — clean it first
Use enough history: 3–5 years minimum
Watch for splits and survivorship bias
For live trading, use your broker's feed

props.caption: yfinance is free and perfect for learning; upgrade to your broker's data later.

props.title: Clean data before you trust it
lines: # sanity: no zero or negative prices

side.title: Cleaning checklist
points: Remove duplicate timestamps
Sort strictly by time
Fill only tiny gaps — never invent data
Reject impossible prices (0 or negative)

props.caption: Ninety percent of 'my bot is broken' turns out to be dirty data.

props.title: Turn raw prices into signals

side.title: What a feature is
points: A number that describes the market now
RSI: is it over-bought or over-sold?
Two averages: is the trend up or down?
Volatility: how wild is it right now?

props.caption: Features are how the market speaks to your model — choose them thoughtfully.

props.title: Look-ahead bias: using the future by accident
lines: # WRONG — this peeks at the future:
#            ^ mean() uses ALL rows, incl. tomorrow
# RIGHT — only use data available at that moment:
df['sig'] = df['Close'] > roll   # past 50 days only
# rule: at row t, touch nothing after row t

side.title: Why it's deadly
points: It makes any backtest look brilliant
It passes tests, then fails live
Rolling/expanding windows fix it
Suspiciously perfect? Check for this first

props.caption: If a backtest looks too good, you almost certainly peeked at the future.

props.title: The model, as a plain rule first

side.title: Why start with a rule
points: You can read and explain every trade
It's a fair baseline to beat later
SEBI calls this a white-box strategy
Most 'AI bots' still end in a line like this

props.caption: Get a transparent rule working end-to-end before you add any AI.

props.title: Test it on history — honestly

side.title: Backtest honestly
points: Always include commission + slippage
No peeking at future bars — ever
A perfect equity curve is a red flag
It's a hypothesis, not a guarantee

props.caption: Set commission realistically — a costless backtest is a fairy tale.

props.title: What the backtest is actually telling you
lines: # few trades = luck. Thousands = costs matter.

side.title: Read it like a pro
points: Ignore return; read risk first
Under ~30 trades? It's noise, not signal
High win rate can still lose to big losers
One number never tells the story

props.caption: A beginner reads the return. A professional reads the drawdown and the trade count.

props.text: Tuning until the backtest looks perfect is how you guarantee it fails live.
props.sub: Every knob you twist to fit the past is a promise the future won't keep.

props.title: Walk-forward: prove it on data it hasn't seen
props.caption: If it survives many unseen windows, you may — may — have something real.

props.title: The honesty test, as a loop
lines: for start in range(0, len(df) - WIN - TEST, TEST):
test  = df[start + WIN : start + WIN + TEST]
r = run(test, params)         # judge on UNSEEN

side.title: The one honest number
points: Optimise on train, score on test — never mix
Roll the window across all history
The median test result is your reality
In-sample numbers are for the bin

props.caption: This tiny loop is the difference between fooling yourself and knowing the truth.

props.title: Judge a strategy by these, not by returns

stats.label: max drawdown you can stomach
stats.src: size positions for the worst case

props.note: Anyone quoting a Sharpe of 8 is overfit, lying, or high-frequency — not you.

props.title: Four checks before you trust a strategy

cards.title: Parameter stability
cards.body: Values near your best should work almost as well. A lone spike is luck.

cards.title: Trade shuffling
cards.body: Reorder the trades randomly; if the worst case ruins you, size smaller.

cards.title: Different periods
cards.body: Test bull, bear, and sideways markets separately.

cards.title: Double the costs
cards.body: If it dies when costs rise a little, the edge was never real.

props.title: The box that keeps you alive
lines: # risk only 1% of capital per trade

side.title: Why this box wins
points: Caps the damage of any single trade
Turns a stop-loss into a share count
Survival first — returns are secondary
This is what pros obsess over

props.caption: You can be wrong most of the time and still win — if this box is right.

props.title: The order box — paper first, always
lines: # same code path for paper AND live —
# run for WEEKS on paper before this touches money

side.title: The going-live ladder
points: 1 — Backtest passes walk-forward
2 — Paper trade for weeks
3 — Go live with tiny size
4 — Scale only what survives

props.caption: The jump from paper to live is where discipline, not code, decides your fate.

props.title: A live bot needs a babysitter

side.title: Non-negotiables for live
points: Log every decision — you'll need the trail
A kill-switch you can hit instantly
Alerts when it errors or loses too much
Handle a dropped connection gracefully

props.caption: A live strategy that no one is watching is an accident waiting to happen.

props.title: Swap the rule for a machine-learning model
lines: # target: did price rise over the next 5 days?

side.title: The AI upgrade
points: The model now sets the rule, from data
Same six boxes — only box 3 changed
Shallow models beat deep ones here
More power = more ways to overfit

props.caption: AI doesn't replace the pipeline — it just makes the model box smarter, and riskier.

props.title: How machine learning fools you
lines: # WRONG — shuffling time series leaks the future
# RIGHT — split by TIME, train on the past only

side.title: ML-specific dangers
points: Never shuffle a time series when splitting
Scale features using train stats only
55% accuracy can be great; 99% is a bug
Predicting price is hard; predicting cost isn't

props.caption: Most ML trading tutorials leak the future. Split by time, or you're lying to yourself.

bullish). Reply with only a number.

side.title: The realistic LLM job
points: Great at reading tone at scale
Feed the score in as one more feature
Watch for look-ahead: use the publish time
It's an analyst, not an oracle

props.caption: The honest LLM use isn't 'predict the price' — it's 'read 10,000 headlines for me'.

props.title: Where LLM agents fit — honestly
Run a portfolio of strategies

cards.title: One bot is fragile
cards.body: When its single edge fades, your whole account fades with it.

cards.title: Several uncorrelated bots
cards.body: When one struggles, another may thrive — smoother overall.

cards.title: Different ideas, not copies
cards.body: Momentum, mean-reversion, and trend behave differently.

cards.title: Allocate by conviction
cards.body: More capital to the proven ones; keep the rest small.

props.text: Every strategy dies. The skill is retiring it before it takes your capital with it.
props.sub: Decide the shutdown rule in advance, when you're calm — not mid-drawdown.
